subject: SOC 2 Type II request — clarification on KMS/key custody and bridge letter
messages:
From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@cypher-audits.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greenleaf.com
Date: 2027-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II report and provider carve-out clarification request — Greenleaf Systems

Hi Sofia,

We're preparing the compliance package for Greenleaf Systems' upcoming vendor review. Can you please provide the following for Redwood Inference: 

- Most recent SOC 2 Type II report (covering the 2026 audit window) or a bridge letter if the period requested by Greenleaf (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31) falls outside your published report.
- A brief statement on whether Redwood relies on cloud provider SOC reports (AWS/GCP) as a carve-out for infrastructure controls, and if so, whether any services are explicitly excluded.
- Confirmation of KMS/key custody model: do you use customer-managed keys, provider-managed keys, or a hybrid approach? Greenleaf needs explicit confirmation re: encryption key custody for data at rest in hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Current subprocessor inventory (names + service scoped) and any subprocessors added/removed in the last 12 months.

If a bridge letter is required, Greenleaf will accept a one-page signed statement identifying covered control buckets and any carve-outs. We can also schedule a short call if helpful.

Thanks — attaching Greenleaf's compliance checklist to show requested evidence types.

Paul Chen
Senior IT Auditor | Cypher Audits
paul.chen@cypher-audits.com
Attachment: Greenleaf-compliance-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@cypher-audits.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and provider carve-out clarification request — Greenleaf Systems

Paul — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Mina (Security) and Karthik (Legal) to help assemble evidence.

Quick answers / next steps from our side:
- We'll attach our latest SOC 2 Type II report (2026) and a draft bridge letter for the requested audit window if the dates fall outside our attestation.
- Redwood does rely on cloud provider SOC reports for certain infrastructure controls. We explicitly do not carve out application-layer controls. We'll provide a short matrix mapping responsibilities (infra vs application) and any excluded services.
- KMS/key custody: see notes below — we need to confirm deployment type: Hosted API, Dedicated (Redwood-managed hw), or Private (customer-managed).
- Subprocessor inventory: attached a current brief CSV export that lists the primary subprocessors and last-changed dates; we'll follow up with the full export.

Could you confirm whether Greenleaf requires the bridge letter to be notarized or just signed by an authorized Redwood officer? Also: are you expecting a vendor-signed confirmation that Redwood uses provider SOC reports as part of the evidence package?

I'll coordinate delivery of the SOC report and a draft bridge letter by EOD tomorrow once Legal signs off. If you'd like a 30-min sync today, propose 11:30am PT.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Attachment: subprocessor-inventory-brief.csv (text/csv)

From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@cypher-audits.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greenleaf.com
Date: 2027-07-01T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and provider carve-out clarification request — Greenleaf Systems

Sofia — thanks. Two clarifications from Greenleaf's side: 

1) AWS/GCP provider reports: Greenleaf's desktop review team wants the vendor to indicate explicitly which control objectives are covered by the provider SOC report (e.g., physical security, environmental controls, change management at the infra layer) and which control objectives Redwood attests to directly. A short responsibility matrix is fine.

2) KMS / key custody: their security team flagged encryption key custody as a blocker if Redwood uses provider-managed keys in the Hosted offering. They need either: (a) confirmation that encryption keys for Greenleaf data are customer-managed (BYOK) for the environment in scope, or (b) a bridge letter indicating compensating controls and the specific controls that remain applicable.

We're fine with a signed one-page bridge letter (no notarization required). The auditor will want the SOC 2 pdf and bridge letter as separate attachments to the compliance packet.

Here's a quick AWS SOC link that Greenleaf references: https://aws.amazon.com/compliance/soc-faq/

We'll plan a short call only if you have open questions after the matrix/attachments.

-Paul
Attachment: Greenleaf-compliance-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@cypher-audits.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-02T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and provider carve-out clarification request — Greenleaf Systems

Paul — thanks for the clarity. Mina and Karthik, please see Paul's notes and proposed action items below.

Quoted for context:
> "KMS / key custody: their security team flagged encryption key custody as a blocker if Redwood uses provider-managed keys in the Hosted offering. They need either: (a) confirmation that encryption keys for Greenleaf data are customer-managed (BYOK) for the environment in scope, or (b) a bridge letter indicating compensating controls and the specific controls that remain applicable."

Action / response (summary we plan to send to Greenleaf):
- SOC 2 Type II: attaching Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (official report).
- Bridge letter: we'll provide a one-page signed bridge letter that explicitly states the audit window coverage and the shared-responsibility split (infrastructure vs Redwood application controls). Draft attached.
- KMS/key custody: Redwood's standard Hosted offering uses Redwood-managed keys (Redwood KMS) — customers on Hosted can elect a Dedicated or Private deployment if they require customer-managed keys. For Dedicated we support customer-provided keys in a BYOK arrangement for tenant-specific volumes; for Private deployments customers manage keys directly. We'll include a short statement in the bridge letter to make this explicit.
- Subprocessors: attaching the current more-detailed inventory and we'll redact contact fields before sending externally.

Please confirm if the wording above satisfies Greenleaf's ask around key custody, or if they require an attestation (signed statement) that we can guarantee BYOK for their account during the audit window. We can update the draft bridge letter accordingly.

Attachments: redwood_bridge_letter_draft.pdf (application/pdf); soc2-type2-redwood-2026.pdf (application/pdf)

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

--
Internal note (not for Greenleaf): Mina/Karthik — please review the draft bridge letter and the KMS language. If Legal prefers different phrasing around "support" vs "guarantee" for BYOK availability, flag before we send.
